templates.label: Raster
templates.description: Render your World into a color image using editable raster shaders.

templates.label: Forward lit
templates.description: Render authored World materials, textures and direct lights with the portable forward profile.

templates.label: Visibility buffer + depth
templates.description: Write original primitive and instance IDs into RGBA8, alongside depth. Exports both attachments with one shared render size. Uses opaque static triangles.

templates.label: Visibility + secondary rays
templates.description: Rasterize visibility and depth, reconstruct the first surface, then trace one reflected secondary ray. Samples authored emission and environment lighting. Requires native ray tracing.

templates.label: ReSTIR DI — mesh emitter lighting
templates.description: Three ray passes with editable shader settings and automatically sized reservoirs. Uses emissive meshes and requires native ray tracing. Temporal reuse has no motion reprojection. Change settings through Properties or the canvas menu.

templates.label: Tiled vbuffer NEE — many-light direct lighting
templates.description: Rasterize visibility, build one emitter-selection table per 16×16 tile, then shade each pixel with a light sample and a BSDF ray, MIS-weighted. Uses emissive meshes and requires native ray tracing.

templates.label: Compute ray tracing — primary hits + direct lighting
templates.description: Two scene compute passes: one records each pixel's primary hit in an automatically sized buffer, the next rebuilds the surface and shades emission plus one shadowed light sample, then Accumulate and ToneMap. Requires native ray tracing.

templates.label: Simple compute ray tracing — triangle loop
templates.description: One compute pass loops over every World triangle, keeps the closest hit and displays its unlit material color plus emission; misses show the environment. No shadow rays or bounces. Uses the native ray-capable scene runtime.

templates.label: Veach & Guibas MIS — light vs BSDF sampling
templates.description: Multiple importance sampling from Veach and Guibas (1995): after a primary-hits pass, three shading passes estimate direct lighting with one light sample and one BSDF sample combined by the balance, power, cutoff or maximum heuristic, with the light sample alone, and with the BSDF sample alone. Each image is accumulated and exported for comparison; the MIS image is shown first. Requires native ray tracing.

templates.label: Line sampling — visible chords of area lights
templates.description: Line sampling from Billen and Dutré (2016): after a primary-hits pass, one shading pass draws a chord across an emissive triangle, finds its visible parts with the scene line query and samples a point on them; a second pass shows the chord's visible fraction (1 lit, 0 in umbra; not radiance). Every pass uses the triangle loop, so it needs Metal or Vulkan compute but no hardware ray tracing.

templates.label: RIS + projected solid angle — many area lights
templates.description: Resampled importance and projected solid angle sampling from Shah, KT and Narayanan (2023): after a primary-hits pass, one shading pass resamples an emissive triangle from power-weighted candidates by its unshadowed LTC shading, samples it with Peters' (2021) projected-solid-angle and LTC techniques, and combines that with a BSDF sample through a surrogate light density; the light strategy alone and the BSDF sample alone are exported beside it. Every pass uses the compute BVH, so it needs Metal or Vulkan compute but no hardware ray tracing.

templates.label: Salesin & Jarosz — point and line samples with MIS
templates.description: Point and line samples combined with MIS, from Salesin and Jarosz (2019): after a primary-hits pass, three shading passes estimate direct lighting with a BSDF sample and line samples in two directions across an emissive triangle, MIS-weighted by the balance or power heuristic; with the two line samples alone; and with a BSDF sample and an area-light point sample. Each image is accumulated and exported for comparison; the combined image is shown first. Every pass uses the triangle loop, so it needs Metal or Vulkan compute but no hardware ray tracing.

templates.label: Peters — BRDF importance sampling for polygonal lights
templates.description: Peters' (2021) comparison of BRDF importance sampling for polygonal lights: four shading passes light every emissive triangle (up to eight) with one projected-solid-angle and one LTC sample combined by clamped optimal MIS (the image shown first), the same two samples with the balance heuristic, the projected-solid-angle sample alone and the LTC sample alone, each with shadow rays. The first pass also records the primary hits for the others. Every pass uses the compute BVH, so it needs Metal or Vulkan compute but no hardware ray tracing.

templates.label: Steinberg — slice sampling a directional luminaire
templates.description: Steinberg's slice sampling for direct light from a near-field directional luminaire: an analytic LED panel of nine tiles with position-dependent Gaussian beams lights the scene. Three shading passes each draw one panel sample with a shadow ray: slice sampling, which turns the panel's emission sampler into a direct-light proposal by solving its seed equation on every tile, in a defensive mixture with uniform panel area (the image shown first); slice sampling alone; and uniform panel-area sampling. The first pass also records the primary hits for the others. Every pass uses the compute BVH, so it needs Metal or Vulkan compute but no hardware ray tracing.

templates.label: Steinberg — partially coherent diffraction
templates.description: Physical light transport from Steinberg and Yan (2021): smooth metals become sinusoidal gratings lit by natural light sources whose finite size sets the light's spatial coherence. After a primary-hits pass, one shading pass renders the gratings' diffraction spectrally (the image shown first), one renders the same gratings in geometric optics, and one shows the coherence radius of the incident light. Other surfaces are shaded classically. Requires native ray tracing.

templates.label: Steinberg — practical physical optics
templates.description: Practical physical-optics rendering from Steinberg, Sen and Yan (2022): camera paths of up to three scattering events carry beams with Stokes vectors and anisotropic Gaussian spatial coherence, scattered by the wave BSDF. Rough surfaces are Gaussian surfaces, dielectrics have a diffuse base and smooth metals are gratings. After a primary-hits pass, one pass renders wave optics (the image shown first), one the same paths radiometrically, and one the coherence length of the incident light. An optional camera polarizer shows polarization. Every pass uses the compute BVH, so it needs Metal or Vulkan compute but no hardware ray tracing.

templates.label: ReSTIR DI — mesh emitter lighting
templates.description: Three ray passes with two automatically sized reservoirs and Graph settings. Connect scene, view and color; requires native ray tracing and emissive meshes.

templates.label: Tiled vbuffer NEE — many-light direct lighting
templates.description: Visibility raster, a per-tile emitter table and an MIS shading pass sharing one automatically sized buffer. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color, visibility and depth. Requires native ray tracing and emissive meshes.

templates.label: Compute ray tracing — primary hits + direct lighting
templates.description: A primary-hits scene compute pass and a shading pass that share one automatically sized hit buffer. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color. Requires native ray tracing.

templates.label: Simple compute ray tracing — triangle loop
templates.description: One compute pass loops over every World triangle, keeps the closest hit and displays its unlit material color plus emission; misses show the environment. No shadow rays or bounces. Uses the native ray-capable scene runtime.

templates.label: Veach & Guibas MIS — light vs BSDF sampling
templates.description: A primary-hits scene compute pass and three shading passes that share one automatically sized hit buffer: MIS of a light and a BSDF sample (Veach and Guibas), the light sample alone and the BSDF sample alone. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color plus optional lightSampling and bsdfSampling images. Requires native ray tracing.

templates.label: Line sampling — visible chords of area lights
templates.description: A primary-hits scene compute pass and two triangle-loop shading passes that share one automatically sized hit buffer: one line sample per pixel over the visible parts of an emitter chord, and the chord's visible fraction. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color plus an optional visibleFraction image. Needs Metal or Vulkan compute.

templates.label: RIS + projected solid angle — many area lights
templates.description: A primary-hits scene compute pass and three compute-BVH shading passes that share one automatically sized hit buffer: resampled emissive-triangle sampling with projected-solid-angle and LTC samples combined with a BSDF sample by MIS, the light strategy alone and the BSDF sample alone. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color plus optional lightSampling and bsdfSampling images. Needs Metal or Vulkan compute.

templates.label: Salesin & Jarosz — point and line samples with MIS
templates.description: A primary-hits scene compute pass and three triangle-loop shading passes that share one automatically sized hit buffer: MIS of a BSDF sample and line samples in two directions (Salesin and Jarosz), the two line samples alone, and a BSDF sample with an area-light point sample. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color plus optional lineSampling and pointSampling images. Needs Metal or Vulkan compute.

templates.label: Peters — BRDF importance sampling for polygonal lights
templates.description: Four compute-BVH shading passes that share one automatically sized hit buffer and light every emissive triangle (up to eight) with Peters' projected-solid-angle and LTC samples: clamped optimal MIS, the balance heuristic, and each technique alone. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color plus optional balanceHeuristic, projectedSolidAngle and ltc images. Needs Metal or Vulkan compute.

templates.label: Steinberg — slice sampling a directional luminaire
templates.description: Three compute-BVH shading passes that share one automatically sized hit buffer and light the scene with an analytic directional LED panel: defensive slice sampling, slice sampling alone and uniform panel-area sampling, each with one shadow ray. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color plus optional sliceSampling and uniformArea images. Needs Metal or Vulkan compute.

templates.label: Steinberg — partially coherent diffraction
templates.description: A primary-hits scene compute pass and three shading passes that share one automatically sized hit buffer: spectral diffraction by smooth-metal gratings under natural light (Steinberg and Yan), the same gratings in geometric optics, and the incident light's coherence radius. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color plus optional geometric and coherence images. Requires native ray tracing.

templates.label: Steinberg — practical physical optics
templates.description: A primary-hits scene compute pass and three shading passes that share one automatically sized hit buffer: physical-optics path tracing with coherence and polarization (Steinberg, Sen and Yan), the same paths radiometrically, and the incident light's coherence length. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color plus optional radiometric and coherence images. Needs Metal or Vulkan compute.

templates.label: Visibility buffer + depth
templates.description: Write RGBA8 primitive/instance IDs and depth. Connect scene, view, visibility and depth; both attachments are exposed as outputs. Uses opaque static triangles.

templates.label: Visibility + secondary rays
templates.description: Rasterize visibility/depth, reconstruct the surface and trace one reflected ray. Connect scene, view and color; outputs color, visibility and depth. Requires native ray tracing.
